newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU Commission report warns of one-off EMU measures.
newsitem.headline: EU Commission report warns of one-off EMU measures.

text.p: The European Commission will says on Thursday that one-off measures taken to help countries meet the requirements of a single currency will not help the objective of sustainable budgetary discipline.

In a report to be released on the European Union's economy, the Commission also will say that it will study the budgets of EU countries in 1998 to see whether durable budgetary restraint has been achieved.

The report, a copy of which was obtained by Reuters, makes no changes to the Commmission's economic outlook for 1997, the year in which countries must bring their budgets into line to qualify for economic and monetary union (EMU).
But its says that one-off efforts being used to meet deficit criteria -- including by Italy and France -- will not help the process of long-lasting budgetary rigour.
"It is is evident that the temporary nature of these (types of) measures does not contribute to improving the fundamental budget situation," the report says.
The Commission will look at how countries have fared in meeting EMU criteria in early 1998, and recommend which should be in the first wave.
